# Copilot Instructions for apocryphalenterprises.com

## Repository Overview

This repository contains the source code and content for the Apocryphal Enterprises website.

## General Guidelines

### Code Quality
- Write clean, maintainable, and well-documented code
- Follow industry best practices for web development
- Ensure all code is production-ready before committing
- Use meaningful variable and function names

### Documentation
- Document all non-trivial functions and components
- Keep README.md up to date with any significant changes
- Include inline comments for complex logic
- Update documentation when making changes to existing features

### Version Control
- Write clear, descriptive commit messages
- Keep commits focused and atomic
- Reference issue numbers in commit messages when applicable

## Development Workflow

### Before Making Changes
1. Review the existing codebase to understand current patterns
2. Check for similar implementations that can be referenced
3. Ensure you understand the full scope of the requested change

### Testing
- Test all changes locally before committing
- Verify that changes don't break existing functionality
- Consider edge cases and error conditions

### Code Review
- Ensure code is self-explanatory or well-commented
- Check for potential security vulnerabilities
- Verify that changes align with the repository's goals

## Best Practices

### Security
- Never commit sensitive information (API keys, passwords, etc.)
- Validate and sanitize all user inputs
- Follow security best practices for web development

### Performance
- Optimize for performance where applicable
- Minimize dependencies
- Consider load times and user experience

### Maintainability
- Write code that is easy to understand and modify
- Avoid over-engineering solutions
- Keep the codebase organized and structured

## Communication

- Provide clear explanations of changes and their rationale
- Ask for clarification when requirements are ambiguous
- Document any assumptions made during implementation

## Additional Notes

This is a growing repository. As the project evolves, these instructions should be updated to reflect new patterns, standards, and requirements.
